MetService issues updated forecasts daily that could shift sentiment ahead of resolution.

Updated IMD forecasts and satellite observations of the monsoon trough position will be key near-term data points.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Japan Meteorological Agency forecasts and ensemble model runs project Tokyo's August 18 high near 31–33 °C under mostly cloudy skies with isolated showers, moderating daytime insolation and surface heating. This consensus drives the near-even split between 31 °C (40.5%) and 30 °C (37.5%), as traders weigh small differences in cloud timing, boundary-layer mixing, and urban heat-island effects against climatological August averages around 31 °C. Lower odds on 32 °C+ reflect reduced solar input from persistent cloud cover, while minimal probabilities below 29 °C align with the absence of stronger cooling mechanisms such as widespread rain or northerly flow. Updated model runs tomorrow morning will refine these thresholds ahead of official resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest Hong Kong Observatory guidance and multi-model consensus indicate a daytime maximum near 31–32 °C for August 18 under humid conditions with scattered showers. Persistent moisture from the regional monsoon trough and embedded thunderstorms can limit solar heating through increased cloud cover and evaporative cooling, keeping peaks from reaching 33 °C or higher. Conversely, brief breaks in convection or localized subsidence may allow temperatures to touch or exceed 32 °C in urban areas. With leading market-implied probabilities tightly clustered between 31 °C and 32 °C, traders are weighing the timing and intensity of any rain relative to the daily temperature cycle against the backdrop of seasonally above-normal warmth. Updated HKO forecasts and radar trends through the morning will likely drive the next shifts in sentiment.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent official forecasts from the Turkish State Meteorological Service and major models place Istanbul’s August 18 maximum near 29–31 °C, aligning with the tightly clustered market outcomes. Mid-August subtropical high pressure and near-peak solar insolation support these readings, while the Bosphorus and Marmara Sea exert a moderating marine influence that typically limits afternoon highs by 1–2 °C through sea breezes and enhanced boundary-layer mixing. Updated model guidance ahead of resolution will clarify whether conditions trend toward the lower or upper end of this narrow range.

**Persistent southwest monsoon activity is the dominant factor capping daytime heating in Metro Manila ahead of August 18.** Official PAGASA guidance shows a 60% chance of rain with forecast highs of 29–32°C under mostly cloudy skies and scattered thunderstorms, consistent with the habagat pattern that has dominated western Luzon through mid-August. These conditions reduce incoming solar radiation and enhance evaporative cooling, keeping maximum temperatures near or below seasonal norms of roughly 30–31°C. 

AccuWeather and extended model runs similarly point to daily peaks in the upper 20s to low 30s Celsius, with limited clearing expected. The market’s heavy weighting toward 28°C (46.5%) and 29°C (36%) therefore reflects trader assessment of ongoing monsoon moisture and cloud cover as the primary controls on the day’s peak reading, with only modest upside risk if breaks in the rain allow brief heating. Updated PAGASA briefings and next model cycles will be the key near-term catalysts.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Marcos A. Gelabert Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 18 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Marcos A. Gelabert Intl Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/pa/panama-city/MPMG.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current short-range model guidance and observational trends position Panama City’s August 18 daily maximum near 30–31 °C, aligning with the market’s closely matched leading outcomes. The rainy season’s Intertropical Convergence Zone drives frequent afternoon convection, producing cloud cover and showers that cap peaks, while clearer morning windows or reduced rainfall allow brief warming toward 31 °C. Historical August climatology shows averages of 30–32 °C with typical ±1–2 °C model spread, underscoring sensitivity to the latest NWP runs and local observations. Traders emphasize timing of any convective initiation and steering influences, as even modest shifts in insolation or moisture could tip resolution between the 30 °C and 31 °C bins.
